You OWN crates/core/src/extractor/** (component.rs, wrapper.rs, evidence.rs, interface.rs, visit.rs, mod.rs, wrapper_matrix_tests.rs) and crates/core/src/resolver/callee.rs only if item C needs it; touch nothing else. 'A test varies what it claims', 'Absence is not evidence', 'Shared state'), docs/architecture/extractor-ast-visiting.md, and `gh pr view 523` (what the last two rounds did: one exhaustive `wrapper()` match, `peel`/`peel_expr`/`callee_of`/`call_type_arguments`/`super_class`, `wrapper_matrix_tests.rs`). Rules: signed commit(s) with trailer `Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/REDACTED`; `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile` first; machine shared (check `uptime`; one cargo process at a time; scratch under /tmp/claude-501/); update the PR body FILE /tmp/claude-501/pr-oxc.md in place (add a 'Review round 3' heading, keep what is true) and I publish it; update the changeset `.changeset/wrapped-component-forms.md` if the user-visible description changes. Final message max 150 words: head SHA, what each item became, blockers. Cap 110 tool calls; never ask questions.

THE THREE FINDINGS (from the Entire reviewer on 5cc72430; verify each against the code, with a test that fails first): (A, low) `export const Root = (Object as typeof Object).assign(Impl, { Item: (props: ItemProps) => <div /> })` now recognises `Root` as a component alias (is_object_assign_call peels the member object) but silently omits `Root.Item`: visit.rs ~343-345 records the alias and runs the inline-member scan, but interface.rs ~410 rejects the cast receiver before it attaches `Item`. Two predicates answer the same question: make the scan use `is_object_assign_call`. (B, medium) `export const Normalize = (props: Props) => (Object as (value: object) => object)(props)` now counts as rendering solely because the peeled callee `Object` is PascalCase, though the assertion gives the call a plain-object result: `renders` accepts it as the arrow's return evidence (evidence.rs ~283-287) and typed-function detection emits a component mapping (component.rs ~367-382, visit.rs ~377-379); base did not match the asserted callee. Do not use the name-only shortcut when the callee assertion explicitly gives the call a non-renderable result. (C, medium) `(wrap as <T>(render: React.FC<T>) => React.FC<T>)<Props>((props: Props) => <div />)`: peeling the assertion lets `wrapper_callee` attach the ORIGINAL `wrap` declaration to the mapping (wrapper.rs ~373-379, component.rs ~482-485); if `wrap` declares `React.FC<T & { internal?: string }>` the resolver looks up that original signature (resolver/callee.rs ~131-149) and prefers it over the callback's `Props` (resolver/mod.rs ~1032-1049), exposing `internal` though the ASSERTED signature hides it. Use the asserted signature for result resolution, or fall back to the detected props when the assertion cannot be resolved.

ROOT CAUSE (do this, not three patches): peeling through an ASSERTION (`as`, `<T>x`) is not transparent for a callee: the assertion REPLACES the callee's type, so what the original binding is called, and what the original declaration says, no longer describe the call. `satisfies`, `!` and parentheses keep the type and are fine. The matrix proved only forms where the asserted type is `typeof` the callee itself (the identity cast), so it never saw an assertion that changes meaning. DESIGN: make `Peeled` carry what the assertion said (e.g. `asserted: Option<&TSType>`, or an enum Identity/Replaced(type)), and one predicate `keeps_identity(peeled)` true only when no assertion was crossed, or the asserted type is `typeof <the same expression>`, `any` or `unknown`; every consumer that uses the callee's NAME (the PascalCase/wrapper-name shortcuts in evidence.rs/component.rs) or its DECLARATION (`wrapper_callee`, resolver callee lookup) must require it, and for a replaced identity must either decline (B: not a rendering call unless the asserted return type is itself a renderable/React type or unresolved named type such as `F`; decide with an allow-list, not a deny-list: AGENTS.md 'allow-lists': unknown stays unknown) or use the asserted type (C: do not attach the original declaration; the detected callback props stand). Sweep EVERY consumer of `peel`/`callee_of`/`call_type_arguments`/`super_class`/`peel_expr` for name or declaration use after an assertion (grep them all, list each in the PR body with its decision) and apply (A) the single `is_object_assign_call` predicate at the inline-member scan and anywhere else `Object.assign` is matched (grep `assign`).

TESTS: (1) a failing-first test per finding with the exact sources above, asserting the exact expected extraction (A: `Root` and `Root.Item` both present; B: no component named `Normalize`; C: the mapping's props are exactly `Props`' and do not contain `internal`). (2) Extend `wrapper_matrix_tests.rs` with NEGATIVE/REPLACING rows: for each detection form, an assertion to a type that is NOT the identity (a function type returning `object`, a function type returning a different component type, `as unknown as X`), with the expected result stated per row (declined, or detected from the asserted type), not 'equals the unwrapped form'; the identity rows (`typeof f`, `any`) stay equal to unwrapped. (3) Mutation-prove `keeps_identity` (make it always true: B and C tests fail; always false: identity rows fail). Verify: output byte-identical (JSON parsed, `stats` dropped) vs a build of origin/main (oxc 0.158) on /Users/gabe/.cache/caliper/corpora/repos/{mantine/packages/@mantine/core/src,chakra-ui/packages/react/src,shadcn-ui/apps/v4,ant-design/components,react-spectrum/packages}; drop runs whose diagnostics hold a SEMANTIC_BACKEND entry with severity other than info (check code and severity, never message text).
